c.tagline: Dutch-built ramparts, boutique cafes, and Indian Ocean sunsets on Sri Lanka's south coast.

taxi.fareNote: Most local trips are by tuk-tuk (three-wheeler), metered through the PickMe app or negotiated in cash. Agree the fare before you set off if paying cash.

emergency.note: 119 reaches the police; 110 is the fire & rescue line; 1990 is the free nationwide Suwa Seriya ambulance service.

avoid.reason: Gem-shop and 'attraction closed today' tuk-tuk scams around the Fort, and strong swimming currents at nearby beaches.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed Dutch fort is the atmospheric heart of Galle — cobbled lanes of restored colonial villas, boutique cafes, art galleries, the lighthouse and rampart walks above the sea. Best for first-timers who want history and character on their doorstep.

A palm-fringed crescent beach about 6 km east of the Fort, packed with beach cafes, dive shops, guesthouses and easygoing nightlife; suits travelers who want swimming and a relaxed seaside base close to the sights.
Galle's workaday city center outside the Fort, around the main bus stand, cricket stadium and market; cheaper and less polished but handy for transport, shopping and everyday local life.

A quieter upscale stretch of coast southeast of Unawatuna with boutique villas, reef-sheltered swimming and a calmer pace; good for couples and those wanting seclusion within a short tuk-tuk of the Fort.
A small, laid-back beach cove famous for its palm-tree rope swing and turtle-spotting, lined with cabana-style guesthouses; suits budget and younger travelers wanting a mellow beach scene.

transit.hours: Local and intercity buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 8:00 PM; the coastal train runs several services daily until early evening. Tuk-tuks are available around the clock.
transit.note: Galle has no metro or tram; getting around relies on buses, tuk-tuks and the scenic Coastal Line railway that hugs the shore between Colombo and Matara.
transit.pay: Bus and train fares are paid in cash (buses to the conductor; train tickets at the station counter). Tuk-tuks are metered through the PickMe app or negotiated in cash.

bus: CTB & private buses along the southern coast and to Colombo
Southern Expressway highway buses to Colombo (~2 hrs)
train: Coastal Line trains north to Colombo and south to Matara

transit.m: Highway coach Colombo–Galle then tuk-tuk (~3 hrs total)
Private taxi via the Southern Expressway (2.5-3 hrs)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a 10% service charge is often already added at hotels and restaurants. Rounding up or leaving ~10% for good service is appreciated.

places.name: Lucky Fort Restaurant

landmarks: Galle Fort
This UNESCO-listed 17th-century Dutch citadel encloses an entire living town of colonial villas, boutiques and cafes behind massive coral-and-granite sea walls.
Galle Fort Ramparts
Circle the fort atop weathered bastions at sunset, when cricket games, kite-flyers and crashing Indian Ocean surf create Sri Lanka's most atmospheric evening stroll.
Galle Lighthouse (Pointe de Galle Light)
Sri Lanka's oldest light station, this photogenic 1939 white tower rises above coconut palms and fort walls at the citadel's southeastern tip.
Dutch Reformed Church (Groote Kerk)
Completed in 1755, this gabled church preserves tombstone-paved floors, an antique organ and the austere elegance of Dutch colonial worship.
Old Dutch Hospital
A beautifully restored colonial arcade overlooking the harbour, the former hospital now hosts breezy restaurants and shops beneath its thick columns and terracotta roofs.
Flag Rock Bastion
The fort's southernmost bastion draws crowds for daredevil cliff jumpers, street food vendors and the finest sunset vantage over the crashing ocean.
National Maritime Museum
Housed in a 1671 Dutch warehouse, its exhibits of shipwreck treasures, maps and marine life chronicle Galle's centuries as a spice-route harbour.
All Saints' Church
This Victorian Anglican church of 1871 adds Gothic-revival spires and stained glass to the fort's skyline of Dutch gables and lighthouse.
Japanese Peace Pagoda (Rumassala)
A gleaming white Buddhist stupa on jungle-clad Rumassala hill, offering serene views back across the bay to Galle Fort and turquoise Jungle Beach below.
Unawatuna Beach
A ten-minute ride from the fort, this famous banana-shaped bay of golden sand and calm reef-protected water is southern Sri Lanka's classic swimming beach.

train.note: The scenic Coastal Line runs north to Colombo Fort (~2.5-3 hrs) and south to Matara, hugging the shoreline much of the way. Galle station sits just outside the Fort walls, a five-minute walk from the ramparts. Most coastal trains are unreserved and tickets are sold at the counter on the day of travel; reserved seats on the few intercity services can be booked via the Sri Lanka Railways portal at seatreservation.railway.gov.lk. Sri Lanka has no cross-border railway of any kind.

bus.note: Frequent CTB and private buses run along the Galle Road and via the Southern Expressway to Colombo (~2 hrs by highway bus), with regular services south to Matara, Mirissa and Tangalle. Expressway coaches leave from the bus stand beside the cricket stadium north of the Fort; fares are paid on board and there is no advance booking. No international coaches operate from Sri Lanka.

ferry.note: Galle Harbour handles cargo, naval vessels, a yacht marina and occasional cruise calls, but there is no scheduled passenger ferry in or out. The boats available to visitors are whale-watching and diving craft, most of them leaving from Mirissa about 45 minutes east, sold through hotels and dive shops rather than on a timetable. Sri Lanka's only international sea link is the Kankesanthurai-Nagapattinam fast ferry in the far north, roughly a full day away.

full.name: Mirissa
full.blurb: Sri Lanka's top blue-whale watching harbour plus a laid-back palm beach, about an hour east.

full.name: Sinharaja Rainforest
full.blurb: UNESCO lowland rainforest reserve with endemic birds and jungle trails, a full day inland.

full.name: Udawalawe safari
full.blurb: Elephant-rich national park for a jeep safari, a long but rewarding day out.
